result: I throttled the login submission using the framework's own rate limiter rather than hand-rolling one. New middleware `app/Http/Middleware/ThrottleLogin.ts` exports `throttleLogin()`, which builds a `createRateLimitMiddleware` at 5 requests per 60 s backed by a per-instance in-memory `LoginThrottleStore` (a `MemoryRateLimitStore` subclass with the store's non-unref'd sweep timer turned off and expired entries swept on each increment instead, so nothing keeps the process alive or grows unbounded); `trustProxy` stays off so the identity is the connection's own peer address and forwarded-for headers are ignored, and the framework's fallback buckets requests whose address can't be resolved under one shared key — fail closed. Over the limit the client gets 429 plus `Retry-After`, including on a submission with the right password, and every submission counts since the counter increments before the controller runs. It is wired only onto `POST /login` in `routes/auth.ts` via the route's `middlewares` option, leaving `GET /login`, registration, and every other route untouched. `tests/LoginThrottle.test.ts` covers the 6th submission getting 429 with a sane `Retry-After`, the form and other pages staying reachable while throttled, spoofed `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-IP` not buying a fresh bucket, and submissions being allowed again after the window (via an injectable clock the middleware accepts for that purpose); `docs/adr/0002-throttle-login-attempts-per-client-ip.md` records the rationale and the multi-instance caveat. `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (5 pass, 0 fail), and `bunx guren check --docs` all pass.
